evidence.excerpt: `test.check(condition)` requires `bool`. `test.equal(actual, expected)` requires identical static types ... A failed assertion exits with status 1. This is a test failure, not a runtime-safety violation, so it does not use the runtime-safety status 101.

For reproducible projects, `quidra package lock FILE.qui` writes `quidra.lock` with the SHA-256 of every direct and transitive installed package actually reached by the import graph. Once present, the compiler enforces those hashes; `quidra package lock FILE.qui --check` is the non-writing CI check.

scorer_notes: Exactly 2 of V1-V6 satisfied, which is the 'Minimal' level (20). Not 40 ('Basic', 3 indicators) because V1, V3, V4 and V5 each fail on directly verified absence of the capability, not on any host limitation: there is no manifest-driven build, no test runner, no coverage facility and no machine-readable test-result format in quidra 0.2.0. Not 0 ('None', 0 or 1 indicator) because two indicators are positively evidenced: the toolchain does ship an admissible first-party test construct (the `test` namespace, used to express TEST-1 and executed here), and its official documentation does state failed-test exit-status semantics and name a non-interactive CI check mode. Direct inspection falsified it for V2 only (the documented `test` namespace), so V2 was awarded and the identical correction rule was applied to every other language in the same position (Java, Kotlin).
